title: A direct summand of a finite free module is finite locally free (standard cover)
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $M$ an $A$-module which is a direct summand of a finite free $A$-module (equivalently, $M$ is finite projective). Then there are finitely many elements $f_1,\dots,f_r\in A$ generating the unit ideal such that for every $i$ the localization $M_{f_i}$ is a finite free $A_{f_i}$-module.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00NX (lemma-finite-projective, line 19027), implication (3)$\Rightarrow$(7) (direct summand of a finite free module $\Rightarrow$ finite locally free), with Definition Tag 00NV of finite locally free

proof.text: View the assumed direct summand of a finite free module as a finite projective module. For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-prime-local-free] to obtain an element $f_{\mathfrak p}\notin\mathfrak p$ for which $M_{f_{\mathfrak p}}$ is finite free over $A_{f_{\mathfrak p}}$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00NX (lemma-finite-projective), implication (3)\Rightarrow(7), the local finite-free neighbourhood construction

proof.text: The principal opens $D(f_{\mathfrak p})$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ because $f_{\mathfrak p}\notin\mathfrak p$. By quasi-compactness of the prime spectrum, choose finitely many of them, say $D(f_1),\ldots,D(f_r)$, still covering. The principal-open/unit-ideal criterion gives that $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ generate the unit ideal, and each corresponding localization $M_{f_i}$ is finite free by the first step.
